lessons.title: Question: Importing React
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which statement imports React into our app?

import React from "react"import "react"import from "react"

import React from "react".
lessons.hardModeContent:
You wrote import { React } from "react", but need the package's default export as React.

Which replacement fixes the import?

import React from "react"import "react"import from "react"import { React } from "react"

Make sure to pick import React from "react".

lessons.title: Example: Importing ReactDOM
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the import statement for React.

Make sure to type React.

lessons.title: Question: index.html
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which HTML tags do we need to include in index.html for this React app to work?

<div id="panel">...</div><div id="me">...</div><div id="main">...</div>

<div id="panel">...</div>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You change the lookup argument from "panel" to "main". Which HTML container matches the changed code?

<div id="main">...</div><div id="panel">...</div><div id="me">...</div><div class="main">...</div>

<div id="main">...</div>.

lessons.title: Example: index.html II
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the correct id to the div container inside the HTML to allow the React content to appear on the page.

Make sure to type id="root".

lessons.title: Example: Attributes
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code src={url} inside the image element to ensure the image is displayed correctly.

Make sure to type src={url}.

lessons.title: a - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Return a paragraph displaying Welcome.

React converts JSX into real HTML, so your browser can understand and display it just like normal HTML.

Make sure to pick return followed by <p> and then Welcome, </p>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create TextComponent to return a paragraph displaying Welcome.

React converts JSX into real HTML, so your browser can understand and display it just like normal HTML.

Make sure to pick TextComponent, followed by return, <p>, Welcome, and finally </p>.

lessons.title: Lesson #16 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the building block of a React app called?

ComponentsFunctionsClasses

Make sure to pick Components.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Your app reuses Header three times. Where should you edit its heading text to update all three displays?

In the JSX returned by the Header component.At each place where the Header component is used.Inside the HTML container passed to createRoot.

In the JSX returned by the Header component.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Import the default exported Greeting component and the named export Footer.

Make sure to pick Greeting followed by { and then Footer, }.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Import Greeting, which has only a default export, and Footer, which has only a named export.

Make sure to pick Greeting, followed by from, {, Footer, and finally }.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make this a default exported component.

Make sure to type default.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What should each React component file begin with?

An import statement for ReactA CSS importA function callA return statement

An import statement for React.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Greeting.jsx imports React. You create a separate component file using the same setup.

Does the new file automatically receive Greeting's React import?

No, add a React import in the new file too.Yes, because both files are in the same folder.Only if the new component is a default export.Only after Greeting is rendered first.

No, add a React import in the new file too.

lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the output of this code?

It displays What will I display? in an h1 tagIt displays What will I display? in an p tagIt displays What will I display? in an span tag

It displays What will I display? in an h1 tag.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You change both h1 tags in MyComponent to p. What displays its text after rendering?

A paragraph displaying What will I display?A heading displaying What will I display?A paragraph displaying MyComponent.The unchanged loading text.

A paragraph displaying What will I display?

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a functional component that displays a list of items.

Make sure to pick const followed by List and then =, (, ), =>, {, }, ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use const and arrow syntax to create List, which displays the items.

Make sure to pick const, followed by List, =, (, ), =>, {, }, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of the export default statement?

To make the component accessible in other filesTo compile the componentTo import styles for the componentTo run the component immediately

To make the component accessible in other files.
lessons.hardModeContent:
List.jsx ends with export default List. What does that let App.jsx do?

Import List and render it in AppRun List immediately without importing itTo import styles for the componentTo run the component immediately

Import List and render it in App.

lessons.title: Lesson #15 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a div element with an id property set to "root" to serve as the container for our React code.

Make sure to pick <div id="root">, followed by </div>.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create a div element with an id property set to "root" to serve as the container for our React code.

Make sure to pick <div id="root">, followed by </div>.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of these paths correctly imports a component named Header from the same directory?

import Header from "./Header";import Header from "../Header";import Header from "Header";import Header from "/Header";

import Header from "./Header";.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You rename Header.jsx to Menu.jsx in the same folder. It still exports Header as default.

Which import loads the renamed file?

import Header from "./Menu";import Header from "../Menu";import Header from "Menu";import Header from "./Header";

import Header from "./Menu";.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Combine the default Content component import with a named export Sidebar.

Make sure to pick export, followed by export, and finally default.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Match the import in App.jsx: export Content as default and Sidebar by name.

Make sure to pick export, followed by Sidebar, export, default, and finally Content.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does ./ signify when importing a component?

The current directoryThe root directoryThe parent directoryAn external library

The current directory.
lessons.hardModeContent:
App.jsx imports ./Header. Where does the path tell the module loader to look first?

The current directoryThe project root directoryThe parent directoryAn external library

Make sure to pick The current directory.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make the Main component the default export.

Make sure to pick export, followed by default.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make Main return its JSX and export that component as the default.

Make sure to pick return, followed by export, default, and finally Main.

lessons.title: a - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the code to make the HobbyComponent work as expected.

Make sure to type return.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the correct tag name for a component in React?

<ComponentName /><componentName /><Component-Name /><component_name />

<ComponentName />.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The component variable is ProfileCard, but your JSX uses <profileCard />.

Which change makes JSX use the component variable?

Use <ProfileCard /> in JSXUse <profile-card /> in JSXRename the variable to profileCard and keep the JSXUse <profile_card /> in JSX

Use <ProfileCard /> in JSX.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
What statement correctly imports a React component from another file?

import App from "./App"require("./App")include "./App"using App from "./App"

import App from "./App".
lessons.hardModeContent:
App.jsx is beside a file whose default export is App. Which statement imports that component?

import App from "./App"import { App } from "./App"include "./App"using App from "./App"

Make sure to pick import App from "./App".

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which of the following is a rule for rendering React components?

Components must start with a capital letterComponents should start with a lowercase letterComponents are written without any letter case preferenceComponents must start with a number

Components must start with a capital letter.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You define a component named ProfileCard. Which naming rule lets React distinguish its JSX tag from a built-in HTML tag?

Components must start with a capital letterComponents should start with a lowercase letter like HTML tagsComponents are written without any letter case preferenceComponents must start with a number

Components must start with a capital letter.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What will happen if we import only one of the named components like this?

Only the Ghost component will be renderedBoth Ghost and Snake components will be renderedAn error occurs for importing SnakeThe app will not render

Only the Ghost component will be rendered.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Trace the imported component through App. What text appears in the root?

Only Boo! from the Ghost componentBoth Boo! and Hissss! because both are exportedAn error because Snake was not imported too.The literal word Ghost.

Only Boo! from the Ghost component.

lessons.title: Lesson #1

Use named exports to create multiple components in a single file.

Make sure to pick export followed by Character and then export, Setting.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Export Character for the Sherlock Holmes text and Setting for the London text, using named exports.

lessons.hardModeContent:

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the correct way to import the default exported Navbar component from Navbar.jsx?

import Navbar from "./Navbar";import { Navbar } from "./Navbar";import "./Navbar";import { default as Navbar } from "./Navbar";

import Navbar from "./Navbar";.

Navbar.jsx replaces its named export with only export default Navbar.

Which import should the file beside it use now?

import Navbar from "./Navbar";import { Navbar } from "./Navbar";import "./Navbar";import Navbar from "../Navbar";

import Navbar from "./Navbar";.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is necessary to import a React component from a different file and use it?

Use the import statementDeclare the component as a global variableUse the require functionUse the component using a direct DOM manipulation

Use the import statement.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Profile.jsx exports a component, and App.jsx needs to render it. What must App.jsx do first?

Use an import statement that points to Profile.jsxDeclare a new global variable named ProfileUse the require functionUse the component using a direct DOM manipulation

Use an import statement that points to Profile.jsx.

lessons.title: Lesson #3

Import the existing Hero component and render it multiple times within the App component.

Make sure to pick import followed by Hero and then from, "./Hero", <Hero />, <Hero />, <Hero />.

Import Hero and render it exactly three times below the heading, with no extra elements or text.

Make sure to pick { followed by Movie and then }, <Movie />.

Import both named exports from Cinema.jsx, listing Movie before Director.

Render the movie before the director.
